correctness.rationale: All prime powers, including characteristic 2, are handled. Distinct-line Gram determinant is nonzero. Nontrivial Mellin blocks are either invertible or rank one according to the character cross-ratio test. The explicit 3x3 constant block has determinant q^2(1_(a nonzero)1_(b nonzero)-1_(c nonzero)), so it contributes precisely the trivial-character nullity exactly in the all-nonzero case. The order of the ratio counts all and only kernel characters. Parameterizing other projective lines by v+z v-perpendicular yields every incidence count with exact odd/even square-root multiplicities. Complete numerical SVD enumeration in eleven small prime/extension fields and independent ratio histograms corroborates the derived formulas; the proof is algebraic.

value.rationale: The union of two through-origin lines is the canonical first multiline Fourier aperture. The exact nullity tells when its own Fourier samples uniquely determine every supported signal, and the explicit kernel modes show what is lost. The projective count and order-refined complete rank distribution are natural finite incidence invariants, uniform for every prime-power field; different orders cause genuinely different nullities. This is more than a single textbook rank deduction, yet no general multiline or condition-number theorem is asserted.
